History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
39-year-old male awoke at 05:30 today with a new, severe left-sided headache unrelieved by paracetamol; telephone assessment suggests migraine or tension-type headache and first-line treatment with ibuprofen plus stress-reduction measures was advised.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Really horrible” left-sided headache that woke patient from sleep this morning.  
• Onset/duration: Began ~05:30 today; continuous and still present at time of call.  
• Character & severity: Worse than any prior headache; previously had milder, usually frontal “cluster”-like headaches.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Mild photophobia (“bright lights make eyes a little bit sore”).  
  – Brief dizziness on first arising; resolved.  
  – No nausea, vomiting, focal neurologic deficits, neck stiffness, or fever.  
• Positional factors: Initially worse on lying down, then partially eases once comfortable; overall slightly better when lying down.  
• Medications tried: Single dose paracetamol this morning – no relief.  
• Triggers/exacerbating factors: Ongoing work stress and late nights for ~2 months; possible sleep deprivation.  
• Relief factors: Rest/lying down offers mild relief.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives unless stated above): No visual aura, speech difficulty, limb weakness, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, recent head trauma, sinus congestion, or infectious symptoms.

Past Medical History:
• Generalised anxiety disorder – diagnosed ~2 years ago; stable.  
  – Medication: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Recurrent mild headaches in past (frontal distribution); no formal migraine diagnosis.  
• Denies hypertension and other chronic illnesses.

Social History:
• Lives with partner; owns a cat.  
• Employment: Experiencing high workload and stress; working late nights for 2 months.  
• Exercise: Runs ~3 times/week.  
• Diet: “OK” – neither particularly healthy nor unhealthy.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol / recreational drugs: Not discussed.  
• No pets other than cat noted.

Family History:
• Mother with anxiety.  
• No family history of migraine or other significant medical conditions reported.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – telephone consultation)  
• No vital signs available.  
• Patient denies neck stiffness, photophobia severe enough to avoid light, or focal neurological deficits.

Investigations:
• None performed or available at this time.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute severe unilateral headache, likely migraine vs tension-type  
Assessment:
– Features supporting migraine: unilateral severe pain, mild photophobia, stress/sleep-deprivation trigger.  
– Features supporting tension-type: prolonged workplace stress, prior frontal “band-like” headaches, partial relief with rest.  
Plan:
1. Pharmacologic:
   • Start ibuprofen (higher-end standard migraine dosing; exact dose/route/frequency not documented).  
   • May continue paracetamol as needed (ensure total dosing within safe limits).  
2. Non-pharmacologic:
   • Ensure ≥7–8 hours sleep nightly.  
   • Maintain hydration ≥1.5–2 L water daily; limit caffeine.  
   • Consider one-week self-certified sick leave to reduce work stress.  
   • Provide link for local self-referral counseling/CBT services.  
3. Education:
   • Provide written information on “red-flag” headache symptoms and when to seek urgent care.  
4. Follow-up:
   • Routine follow-up in 1 week; sooner if worsening, new neurologic signs, vomiting, visual changes, or other concerns.  
5. Contingency:
   • If no improvement, consider in-person exam, vitals, blood tests, and further headache work-up.

Issue 2 – Chronic anxiety (stable)  
Assessment:
– Ongoing but manageable; current stress appears situational.  
Plan:
• Continue sertraline (dose not documented).  
• Encourage engagement with counseling services mentioned above.  
• Monitor mood and anxiety at follow-up; assess for any deterioration or suicidal ideation.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood  
   • Unilateral severe pain, photophobia, stress/sleep deprivation trigger; no focal deficits.  
2. Tension-type (stress-related) headache – Moderate likelihood  
   • Work stress, history of anxiety, prior similar headaches; however current episode is more severe and unilateral.  
3. Cluster headache – Low-moderate likelihood  
   • Early-morning unilateral pain in a male; lacks autonomic features (tearing, rhinorrhoea).
